text:
Premier League predictions & Jones Knows' best bets: Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea, Arsenal vs Manchester City and more!
Watch Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea, Ipswich vs Aston Villa, Crystal Palace vs Hull, Brighton vs Newcastle, Fulham vs Bournemouth, Sunderland vs Tottenham and Arsenal vs Manchester City all live on Sky Sports; play Super 6 on SUNDAY to win £1m!
Thursday 26 November 2026 16:35, UK
Our top tipster Lewis Jones, aka Jones Knows, provides his analysis and betting insight across the Premier League.
Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea, Friday 8pm, live on Sky Sports
I'm not for jumping off the Nottingham Forest bandwagon just yet.
Forest have taken just four points from their last seven Premier League games - no team has taken fewer - yet they sit sixth in the expected points table for the season.
There is a significant disconnect between performance levels and results, something that usually corrects itself over time. I'm still a firm believer that Oliver Glasner will get this talented group of players motoring up the Premier League table.
And I'm struggling to see why Chelsea should command quite so much respect from the markets.
Of the ever-present Premier League teams in 2026, only one has lost more games than Chelsea (14) and only one has conceded more goals (51).
Where has Xabi Alonso's defensive magic gone?
His invincible Bayer Leverkusen side conceded just 24 league goals across their entire title-winning campaign in 2023/24. Chelsea have shipped 20 in 11 games this season alone. There is a softness to this Chelsea team when opponents turn up the intensity and attack them directly.
Just two clean sheets in their last 27 Premier League games tells a sorry tale.
Forest have the attacking weaponry to expose those defensive deficiencies.
The 29/20 with Sky Bet for a home win makes lots of sense.
SCORE PREDICTION: 2-1
Leeds vs Coventry, Saturday 3pm
When the numbers and the theory marry up in the player fouls markets, I'm usually willing to get stuck in. And there is a lovely little match-up brewing down Leeds' right flank that Sky Bet may have underestimated.
Jayden Bogle is an all-action footballer. He's busy, aggressive and covers plenty of ground, which brings him into contact with opposition players at both ends of the pitch. That is exactly the profile of player I like to get onside in the fouls markets.
Across his last 30 games for Leeds, Bogle is averaging 1.75 fouls per 90 minutes. A solid enough starting point when assessing the 10/11 with Sky Bet for him to commit two or more fouls - but it's the opposition that really gets me excited.
Coventry's Yann Gboho is a foul-drawing maestro.
Across his last 50 appearances for Coventry and Toulouse, the tricky winger has been fouled at a rate of 2.2 per 90 minutes, winning eight fouls across his last three appearances for Coventry.
There is plenty of juice in that 10/11 considering this bet has won in four of Bogle's last five games.
SCORE PREDICTION: 2-0 | JONES KNOWS' BEST BET: Jayden Bogle to make two or more fouls (10/11 with Sky Bet)
Manchester United vs Brentford, Saturday 3pm
There are certain footballers you want on your side when playing the cards markets. Lisandro Martinez is very much one of them.
The Argentine looks a walking accident at times for Manchester United, such is his desire to engage physically with opposition players. But throw him into a left-back role and his chances of falling foul of the referee increase significantly.
His natural instinct is to get tight and aggressive rather than stand off his opponent - as we saw with the foul he gave away in Sporting Lisbon that led to a penalty. That's a dangerous game to play against someone with the explosive qualities of Dango Ouattara.
The Brentford winger is developing quite the reputation as a card magnet for opposition defenders.
Since the start of the 25/25 season, Ouattara has drawn a card from an opponent every 199 minutes - that's 14 cards in total. Only Crysensio Summerville (118 mins per card) has a better strike-rate.
Those are impressive numbers and his directness with the ball should make for uncomfortable viewing for Martinez. Ouattara was responsible for getting Vitaliy Mykolenko booked in Monday's win over Everton, too.
The 7/2 with Sky Bet for Martinez to have his name taken looks a price worth attacking.
SCORE PREDICTION: 2-1 | JONES KNOWS' BEST BET: Lisandro Martinez to be carded (7/2 with Sky Bet)
Ipswich vs Aston Villa, Saturday 5.30pm, live on Sky Sports
There is a rather large gap between perception and reality when it comes to Ipswich.
Eleven points from 11 games looks a perfectly acceptable return for a newly promoted team. But scratch beneath the surface and things look considerably more worrying.
Ipswich's expected goals supremacy figure of -0.81 per 90 minutes is the second worst in the Premier League. When assessing their performance when matches are level, that figure drops to -0.98 - the worst in the division.
Their reliance on Julio Enciso to provide attacking inspiration is another concern. Shut him down and Ipswich can become painfully predictable.
Enter Unai Emery, who is unbeaten in 10 games away from home against newly promoted opposition with Villa.
There are very few managers I'd rather have onside when backing a team to expose the obvious tactical weaknesses of an opponent. The 10/11 with Sky Bet for the away win is worth taking.
SCORE PREDICTION: 0-2 | JONES KNOWS' BEST BET: Aston Villa to win (10/11 with Sky Bet)
Everton vs Liverpool, Sunday 12pm - PLAY SUPER 6 TO WIN £1M!
A Merseyside derby before most people have tucked into their Sunday roast? I'm not sure we're going to be treated to a feast of attacking football.
These fixtures rarely deliver in terms of goalmouth entertainment anyway, with the last 14 Merseyside derbies averaging just 2.2 goals per game. And the unusual kick-off time could further contribute to a lack of intensity, both on the pitch and in the stands.
I've dug into the numbers surrounding major English derby fixtures played at this time on a Sunday. Across the seven instances involving the north London derby, the Tyne-Wear derby and Manchester United vs Liverpool kicking off before 12.30pm, under 3.5 goals has landed every time.
It's a small sample but one that marries up nicely with the theory.
To get some juice into the price, I'm adding Alexander Isak to register a shot on target through the Bet Builder, which gets us to Evens with Sky Bet.
Isak is starting to look like the devastating centre-forward we know he can be. He's registered a shot on target in 11 of his last 12 games, including five across his last two.
SCORE PREDICTION: 1-1
Brighton vs Newcastle, Sunday 2.05pm, live on Sky Sports - PLAY SUPER 6 TO WIN £1M!
One of my favourite player markets to attack with Sky Bet is foul involvements when the numbers add up. For those unfamiliar with the market, it's simply a player's fouls committed and fouls won numbers added together. It opens up plenty of opportunities when you can identify a particularly physical individual battle.
And there's one brewing between Luka Vuskovic and Will Osula.
Osula is a proper handful. He's a powerful, willing runner who relishes the physical side of being a centre-forward. Across his last 25 starts, he's averaged 2.70 foul involvements per game.
Throw into the equation a centre-back in Vuskovic who averages 2.72 foul involvements per game for Brighton since joining from Tottenham and we've got all the ingredients for a busy afternoon for the referee.
Anyone who watched Vuskovic's battle with Oliver McBurnie last weekend will know exactly where I'm coming from. It was brutal at times. Vuskovic racked up seven foul involvements as neither player was willing to give an inch.
I'd expect plenty of grappling, shirt-pulling and wrestling when these two come together. Vuskovic's foul involvements is a market worth monitoring with Sky Bet.
SCORE PREDICTION: 2-0
Crystal Palace vs Hull, Sunday 2.05pm, live on Sky Sports - PLAY SUPER 6 TO WIN £1M!
The new manager bounce is a rather fluffy concept. But there is some substance to it when digging into the numbers, especially when the new man in the dugout has home advantage.
Backing the home team in each of the last 30 Premier League matches where a newly appointed manager has taken charge of his first game in the competition for that club would have returned a profit of 9.04 points to level stakes, with 14 wins.
But what really got my betting juices flowing was that 10 of those 14 home wins came with a clean sheet.
Why? Well, my hypothesis is that the quickest way for a new manager to put his stamp on a team is to address their defensive structure. Thomas Frank has openly admitted that defensive organisation is high on his list of priorities at Crystal Palace.
And he could hardly have handpicked a more accommodating opponent in that regard.
I've got plenty of respect for Hull and their ability to squeeze results out of games but their attacking process remains the worst in the Premier League. They rank bottom for expected goals, big chances created and touches in the opposition box.
That makes the 5/2 with Sky Bet for Palace to win to nil a very attractive betting proposition. Frank can get the Selhurst Park faithful onside by keeping things simple.
SCORE PREDICTION: 2-0 | JONES KNOWS' BEST BET: Crystal Palace to win to nil (5/2 with Sky Bet)
Fulham vs Bournemouth, Sunday 2.05pm, live on Sky Sports - PLAY SUPER 6 TO WIN £1M!
My colleague Adam Bate wrote a fantastic piece about Fulham's man-to-man marking tactics up against Erling Haaland, offering up some huge pointers for us punters who like to dabble in the player fouls and cards markets.
Alvaro Arbeloa wants his defenders to engage, get tight and make life as uncomfortable as possible for opposition forwards, even if that means following them into areas of the pitch where centre-backs wouldn't usually venture.
Calvin Bassey is having a fantastic season playing this way. He's got the physical attributes to thrive in such a system but there is an occupational hazard attached to defending with that level of aggression. He's already picked up four yellow cards this season.
And the identity of his likely opponent here makes the 3/1 with Sky Bet for Bassey to be carded a very appealing price.
Evanilson is a master at using his body to manufacture fouls, inviting contact from defenders before rolling them. Since the start of last season, the Bournemouth striker has drawn a card from an opposition player every 267 minutes.
SCORE PREDICTION: 1-2 | JONES KNOWS' BEST BET: Calvin Bassey to be carded (3/1 with Sky Bet)
Sunderland vs Tottenham, Sunday 2.05pm, live on Sky Sports - PLAY SUPER 6 TO WIN £1M!
The Tottenham defensive revolution under Roberto De Zerbi remains one of the more fascinating developments of this Premier League season. There is a perception associated with De Zerbi's football that it will always produce chaotic matches with chances flowing at both ends.
The numbers have been telling a rather different story.
Across his time in charge of Spurs, their expected goals against figure is operating at 1.03 - a figure that ranks them second only to Arsenal over that period. That's a very impressive foundation, particularly for a team whose reputation remains associated with defensive shortcomings.
The absence of European football should increasingly become a significant advantage for Tottenham as the schedule intensifies, too.
Sunderland's attacking troubles make this a particularly attractive opportunity to exploit Spurs' defensive improvement. A Spurs win to nil has a chance at 5/2 with Sky Bet.
SCORE PREDICTION: 0-1
Arsenal vs Manchester City, Sunday 4.30pm, live on Sky Sports - PLAY SUPER 6 TO WIN £1M!
Stuart Pearce was in the Manchester City dugout the last time they endured a Premier League run as bad as the one they'll be on if Arsenal beat them here - one point from five games.
City have won inside 90 minutes in just one of their last seven games across all competitions and look horribly vulnerable without the ball.
Stability is proving elusive for Enzo Maresca. He's used eight different back-four combinations across City's last 10 games in all competitions, tinkering with his defensive personnel from one game to the next. Not a single clean sheet has been forthcoming and they've shipped 20 goals in that period.
Arsenal are worthy favourites but the way to inject some juice into their price is through Noni Madueke.
He's grasped the opportunity presented to him by Bukayo Saka's absence. What he did to Lewis Hall at St James' Park was particularly impressive considering the Newcastle full-back had kept Lamine Yamal relatively quiet for England just a few days earlier.
There is an explosiveness to Madueke's game that makes him capable of creating chances without Arsenal having to dominate territory or possession - something that should be particularly valuable here.
He's registered a goal or assist in three of his last four games. Combining that outcome with an Arsenal win at 15/8 with Sky Bet appeals greatly.
SCORE PREDICTION: 2-1
Jones Knows' best bets...
- Jayden Bogle to make two or more fouls (10/11 with Sky Bet)
- Lisandro Martinez to be carded (7/2 with Sky Bet)
- Aston Villa to win (10/11 with Sky Bet)
- Crystal Palace to win to nil (5/2 with Sky Bet)
- Calvin Bassey to be carded (3/1 with Sky Bet)
